digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate, close-path precheck, attestation validation
propositions: [operator-attested] tag on code-verifiable ACs with exact repo path/symbol evidence bypassed all layered guards and was accepted at close on epic fb8a-7363-e406-4e36, reaching the completion verifier which classifies solely from the tag per ADR-0043

Evidence-kind routing criterion on the re-review run did not detect the tagged repo-provable AC despite its prose citing tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py verbatim; an LLM judgment miss with no deterministic backstop
det_measurement_provenance detected missing provenance lines but was wired to p6_ac_quality (ADVISORY contract), so tagged ACs lacking provenance: continuation lines were not rejected before close

A deterministic pre-LLM close-path guard must fire on [operator-attested] ACs whose own block text cites exact repo paths/symbols (src/, tests/, code-extension slash paths, pytest ::node ids) to reject the laundering anti-pattern before the completion verifier accepts the tag at face value

Mixed-evidence false positives occur when a tagged AC cites a repo path for orientation context (not proof) alongside external evidence; citations must be judged per-line with evidence-introducing words (proxy/proof/evidence/verified/covered/documented) to distinguish orientation from repo-verifiable claims

Untag or split operations on tagged ACs stale the signed plan-review attestation and trigger re-review with rebar review-plan; this re-review cycle must be documented in block messages so post-certification retagging cannot silently escape attestation invalidation
